input.body:
label: bug
file: none

The weekly summary scheduling appears to not correctly account for user time zones relative to UTC/server time, causing users in time zones ahead of the scheduling reference (e.g. Sydney, UTC+10/11) to receive their Monday email a day late, while those closer to the reference time zone (e.g. London) receive it on time. Unable to pinpoint the exact responsible file via search, as the expected job files (src/jobs/weeklySummary.js, src/jobs/sendWeeklySummary.js) do not exist in the repository under those paths. Further investigation into the actual scheduling/cron job implementation is needed to identify the correct file.

text:
label: question
file: none

The weekly summary scheduling appears to mishandle user time zones relative to UTC/server time: users ahead of the reference zone (e.g. Sydney, UTC+10/11) get their Monday email a day late, while users closer to the reference zone (e.g. London) get it on time. Account-level time zone settings are confirmed correct, so the issue likely lies in how the job computes "Monday" for each user.

I couldn't locate the responsible code via search — the expected paths (src/jobs/weeklySummary.js, src/jobs/sendWeeklySummary.js) don't exist in the repo, and no other matches turned up for the scheduling/cron logic. Can someone point to where the weekly summary job is actually defined so we can confirm the time zone handling there?
